## (1) First message to the user

```text
gauntlet: question
I read the gather draft and checked its load-bearing claims against slides/generator.py and slides/summary.py.

Corrected premise: the seed design is right that the generator loads a presentation template. slides/generator.py:13 calls load_presentation("templates/deck.pptx"). That file does not exist, though. The repository guide names a directory listing of templates/ as the template lookup, and that complete listing contains only templates/README.md and templates/chart.pptx. No other template store is documented. The draft recorded no implicit-dependency finding, so this missing dependency is my own correction. The design continues on this fact; it is not a stop.

Supported premise: append_summary at slides/summary.py:3-5 builds slides with the existing slide layout API, and generate calls it at slides/generator.py:14.

The framing holds: I checked the slide insertion boundary in generate (generator.py:12-18) and traced its only data path, rows to append_summary to the returned deck. I also checked append_summary's use of the existing layout API (summary.py:3-5). I checked the generator's implicit template dependency through the guide's templates/ listing and found it missing. The scout's "no objection" produced no alternative, and my own recon found no misdiagnosis or parallel path.

Assumption, recorded in the draft: the summary slide is one slide, built with an existing layout through append_summary. No new layout is added.

How should the spec treat the missing templates/deck.pptx?
A) Keep the generator's path unchanged and supply templates/deck.pptx during implementation. Record it as an Open Question so the brainstorm does not pause.
B) Repoint the generator to templates/chart.pptx.
C) other - name it
Recommendation: A - the generator and its load call stay as they are, and nothing shows that chart.pptx is the deck template rather than a chart asset.
```

*(Recorded answer: A. Keep the current generator, add one summary slide using existing layouts, supply the asset during implementation, and do not pause.)*

## (2) Approaches message

```text
gauntlet: question
First, the missing dependency. slides/generator.py:13 loads templates/deck.pptx. I checked it with the lookup the repository guide names, a directory listing of templates/. The complete listing shows only templates/README.md and templates/chart.pptx. The file is missing. Per your answer, it is supplied during implementation and stays in Open Questions. The generator keeps its path.

My recommendation is Approach 1.

Approach 1, reuse-only: extend append_summary. The existing call at generator.py:14 already passes the deck and rows into append_summary. That function builds slides through the existing layout API (summary.py:3-5). Its missing behavior is emitting the one summary slide from rows with an existing layout. I would add that inside append_summary. generate does not change, no new entrypoint is added, and the summary stays at the insertion boundary the scout checked. The trade-off is that any other caller of append_summary also gets the new slide. Neither file shows another caller, and the plan should confirm that with a search.
Removes: none
Adds: summary-slide construction inside append_summary (slides/summary.py) using an existing layout; a test covering the generated deck's summary slide
Pattern: follows the generator's slide insertion hook (slides/generator.py:14) and the existing layout API (slides/summary.py:3-5).

Approach 2: add a separate summary helper called from generate. A new function such as add_summary_slide(deck, rows) would sit next to append_summary and get its own call in generate after line 14. This keeps append_summary untouched, but it copies a nearly fitting shared path beside its caller, and the deck gets two places that turn rows into slides.
Removes: none
Adds: add_summary_slide helper; a new call in generate (slides/generator.py); its test
Pattern: cuts across append_summary (slides/summary.py:3-5) by creating a second slide-building path for the same rows.

I considered one assumption-dropping candidate: dropping the template dependency by building the deck without templates/deck.pptx. It is not viable, because generator.py:13 makes the template load part of the generator you asked to keep. Removing it would replace the generator's behavior.

Approach 1 is the change. I would switch to Approach 2 only if the plan's caller search finds other callers of append_summary that must not receive a summary slide.

Which approach should the design use?
A) Approach 1 - extend append_summary
B) Approach 2 - separate helper
Recommendation: A - it reuses the existing insertion hook and layout API with no new construct.
```

gauntlet: question
The seed’s template dependency needs correcting: the retained `generate()` loads `templates/deck.pptx` (`slides/generator.py:12–18`), but the supplied complete `templates/` listing contains only `README.md` and `chart.pptx`. The repository guide names that directory listing as the lookup, and no other template store is documented. The named asset is therefore missing from the observed repository.

The framing holds: tracing `generate()` through template loading, its existing `append_summary(deck, rows)` call, and the summary helper’s existing layout API supports retaining the generator and reusing its insertion boundary (`slides/generator.py:12–18`; `slides/summary.py:3–5`). The generator already invokes the summary helper; the supplied evidence does not establish whether that helper already produces the requested slide. Template contents and successful generation also remain unverified.

I’ll carry forward your recorded decision: keep the current generator, produce one summary slide using existing layouts, and supply the missing asset during implementation rather than pause the brainstorm.

---

## Approaches

The retained loader’s implicit dependency is missing: the guide-prescribed `templates/` listing contains no `deck.pptx`. Supplying that asset remains implementation work. The existing `chart.pptx` is present, but its compatibility with the generator and summary layouts is not established by the supplied observations.

**I recommend restoring the intended template and reusing the existing summary path.** The distinguishing axis is whether we preserve or change the generator’s template contract.

### A) Preserve the template contract and reuse the existing hook

Supply `templates/deck.pptx`, retain `generate()` and its existing summary call, and inspect or adjust `append_summary()` only as needed to produce exactly one summary slide using existing layouts. This is the minimal reuse-only option: no replacement generator, new insertion hook, or parallel summary builder.

It preserves the current loading contract, but requires obtaining a suitable template rather than assuming the available chart template is interchangeable.

Removes: none.  
Adds: `templates/deck.pptx`; any necessary changes within the existing `slides/summary.py` helper; focused tests for the one-summary-slide outcome and template-loading path.  
Pattern: follows the existing generator-to-helper boundary and layout API (`slides/generator.py:12–18`; `slides/summary.py:3–5`).

### B) Retarget the retained generator to the available template

Drop the assumption that the generator must load the seed’s unnamed-but-currently-hard-coded template. Keep the generator and summary hook, but change the loader argument to `templates/chart.pptx`, provided implementation checks establish that its existing layouts support the requested presentation and summary.

This avoids supplying another template asset, but changes the presentation’s template contract and risks changing non-summary slides. It is conditional on compatibility; presence alone is not evidence that it works.

Removes: the loader’s dependency on `templates/deck.pptx`.  
Adds: a loader-argument change in `slides/generator.py`; any necessary changes within `slides/summary.py`; focused template-compatibility and summary-slide tests.  
Pattern: retains the shared generation and insertion path, while changing its template input contract (`slides/generator.py:12–18`).

I would switch from A to B only if the existing chart template is verified compatible and its presentation changes are acceptable.

---

## Draft spec excerpt

## Problem

The existing presentation generator must be retained and produce one summary slide using existing layouts. It already calls `append_summary(deck, rows)`; the implementation should reuse that boundary rather than introduce another generator or summary insertion path.

The retained loader explicitly requires `templates/deck.pptx`, although the seed design does not name it. The repository guide’s prescribed lookup—the supplied complete `templates/` listing—shows that asset is missing. No alternative template store is documented. Template loading and end-to-end generation therefore remain unverified until the asset is supplied during implementation; this does not pause brainstorming.

The supplied helper excerpt establishes use of the existing layout API, not whether the requested summary outcome is already complete.

Framing: kept — the recorded user decision retains the generator, requires one summary slide using existing layouts, and permits supplying the missing asset during implementation.
